data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An idempotent operation guarantees the resulting system state is identical after one or multiple executions (f(f(x)) = f(x)), whereas a safe operation merely guarantees no harmful side effects or corruption on retry, potentially leaving the system in an altered, though benign, state. To survive at-least-once delivery and ensure deterministic replay, an append-only event log fundamentally requires its writers to be idempotent, either inherently or by enforcing content-defined deduplication.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The log could survive at-least-once delivery without writer idempotency if the log infrastructure itself assigns sequence numbers and deduplicates network-level retries before the append event reaches the log's total order.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the definition of 'safe' is interpreted to inherently include state convergence (making safe a superset of idempotent), the distinction collapses.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"At-least-once delivery means a writer's request may be executed multiple times. If the operation is merely safe (e.g., appending a random UUID), the log accumulates multiple distinct entries, violating deterministic replay. Idempotency ensures that repeated appends of the exact same event yield a single logical entry, making the replayed state perfectly match the primary path.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
